articles.summary: I have spent much of my career helping teams build trust and work together effectively. Along the way, I have learned an important lesson: productive collaboration starts long before the work itself. It starts with how we meet.
articles.title: The Most Valuable Resource We Share in Meetings Isn’t Information. It’s Time.

articles.summary: Most employees only think about IT systems when something goes wrong. The reality is that systems administrators spend most of their time making sure problems never happen in the first place.
articles.title: Celebrating System Administrators Day: The Experts Who Keep Business Moving

articles.summary: When people think about innovation, they often think about new products or breakthrough technologies. Some of the most meaningful innovations are the ones nobody ever sees. Recently, I had the opportunity to stand alongside a customer team as we validated a solution to a challenge we had been working to solve together for years.
articles.title: The Innovation No One Will Ever See

articles.summary: We know that meaningful progress often starts with simple actions. Earlier this summer, employees at our site in Berlin, Germany, participated in the Bike-to-Work Challenge 2026, a two-week initiative organized by our Environmental Sustainability affinity group and Sustainability team. The goal was straightforward: encourage employees to choose cycling over driving whenever possible and experience the benefits of a healthier, more sustainable commute
articles.title: Small Rides, Big Impact: How Our Berlin Team Turned a Bike Commute into a Sustainability Success Story

articles.summary: Many leadership teams assume that if they are delivering results, they already have everything they need to succeed. The reality is that even high-performing teams can become stronger. That was one of the key lessons from a recent Cohesive Teams experience involving a global leadership team responsible for supporting advanced surgical technologies. Although team members had worked together for years and maintained strong working relationships, the process revealed opportunities to deepen trust and improve communication to strengthen collaboration.
articles.title: Why High-Performing Teams Still Need to Invest in Trust

articles.summary: We recently attended the inaugural MACHINA Summit in Paris, where robotics leaders, AI innovators and automation experts gathered to discuss the future of physical AI.
articles.title: What MACHINA Summit Paris Revealed About the Future of Physical AI

articles.summary: One of the things I enjoy most about working at our company is collaborating with people from around the world. On our Sustainability team, projects regularly involve employees across multiple countries and cultures. Every conversation is a chance to learn something new, not just about the work itself, but about how people communicate and solve problems.
articles.title: Better Ideas Begin with Better Understanding

articles.summary: When I moved from Costa Rica to Berlin, Germany, to join Novanta a year and a half ago, I was excited for a new adventure. What I did not expect was how meaningful it would be to one day stand in front of coworkers and share a piece of home with them. Recently, I had the opportunity to host a Costa Rica-themed event through our Multicultural employee resource group (ERG). What began as a cultural presentation became a powerful reminder of how much it means to feel seen, valued, and connected when you are far from home.
articles.title: Finding Belonging Far from Home: How Sharing Costa Rica Brought Us Closer Together

articles.summary: Recently, our CEO had the opportunity to visit our El Monte, California, site, where we manufacture strain gauges and force-torque sensors. The visit reinforced something we believe strongly: Innovation doesn’t end when we design a product. Real impact comes when we can scale that innovation. Our force-torque sensors are enabling some of the most exciting applications in robotics today, including humanoid robots, minimally invasive and robotic […]
articles.title: Scaling the Technologies That Will Power Physical AI

articles.summary: Creating a positive impact in our communities goes beyond the work we do every day. It also means finding opportunities to support the people and organizations that help our communities thrive.
articles.title: Giving Back Through Action: Supporting Our Community Through a Vitalant Blood Drive

articles.summary: Recognition comes in many forms. Sometimes, it arrives in the shape of a scoop of ice cream shared with coworkers on a summer afternoon. On July 14, our teams in Ludwigsstadt and Sonneberg, Germany, came together to celebrate a successful second quarter with a special treat from a nearby organic farm known throughout the region for its handcrafted ice cream.
articles.title: More Than Ice Cream: Celebrating the People Behind a Strong Quarter

articles.summary: When organizations talk about global collaboration, the focus often lands on challenges, such as time zones or communication styles. Each culture has such different ways of working. The reality is more powerful: When we understand and align across cultures, those differences become a competitive advantage.
articles.title: Global Teams, Stronger Outcomes: How Cultural Differences Drive Better Execution

articles.summary: Across many of the industries we serve, the rules are changing.The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is driving demand for increasingly sophisticated, printed circuit boards, where laser-drilled hole counts can now reach hundreds of thousands, and in some cases approach a million per board.
articles.title: The Future of Precision Manufacturing Starts with People

articles.summary: People often ask whether One Novanta is a program or a framework. While it influences many of our decisions, I think of it differently. One Novanta is a mindset. It is a shared commitment to look beyond our individual teams, sites, business units, and functions and recognize that we are all contributing to something bigger than ourselves.
articles.title: What One Novanta Means to Me

articles.summary: On July 24, employees from our site in Ludwigsstadt, Germany, stepped away from their usual work routines and into nature for a Volunteer Time Off (VTO) day focused on giving back to the local community.Fourteen employees representing four different departments came together to maintain a hiking trail near the site that we proudly sponsor. The trail is a popular destination for local residents and visitors, winding through the beautiful landscapes of the Franconian Forest.
articles.title: Preserving a Local Treasure in the Franconian Forest

articles.summary: Some of the most meaningful community impact doesn't happen in a manufacturing facility. Sometimes it happens on a Monday morning, unpacking boxes of fresh produce alongside coworkers while preparing food for local families. Recently, I had the opportunity to volunteer at the Billerica Community Pantry with a group of employees from our site in Bedford, Massachusetts. The experience left a lasting impression on me, not only because of the important work being done there, but because it reminded me of the value of investing in the communities around us.
articles.title: Giving Back Close to Home: What I Learned Volunteering at the Billerica Community Pantry

articles.summary: Several years ago, I started asking a question that many improvement projects begin with: Why are we doing it this way? The question centered on real-time aging studies, which are an essential part of demonstrating that medical products remain safe, effective, and compliant throughout their shelf life. At the time, much of that testing was performed externally, which meant additional costs and scheduling constraints, along with less flexibility.
articles.title: Building Capability for the Future: Why We Invested in a Real-Time Aging Chamber

articles.summary: Most companies talk about customer focus. Fewer truly practice customer intimacy. There is a difference. Customer focus is responding to what customers ask for. Customer intimacy is understanding what they actually need, even before they say it.
articles.title: From Insight to Impact: Why Customer Intimacy Drives Innovation

articles.summary: When Riverpoint officially joined our company, we knew Day One should be more than an announcement. It should be a celebration. Riverpoint has built an impressive business through innovation and a culture of continuous improvement. Day One was an opportunity to celebrate those achievements and recognize the talented people behind them.
articles.title: More Than an Acquisition: Celebrating a New Chapter Together

While the project delivered important technology and process improvements, what impressed me most was the collaboration and dedication displayed throughout the journey.

articles.summary: ne question has guided much of our work on artificial intelligence: How can we use AI to make it easier for customers to do business with us? For our robotics and automation business, that question led us to tackle a significant challenge. Our product portfolio includes more than 70,000 SKUs and millions of potential configurations. Finding the right solution requires a deep understanding of product specifications, application requirements, and compatibility across a broad range of options. Historically, customers relied heavily on our application engineering teams to navigate that complexity.

Over the years, I've learned that understanding those differences can strengthen collaboration, but only if we approach them with the right mindset. That's why I found the Culture Map Assessment valuable.
